evidence: Ov. Met. 1.304: nat lupus inter ovēs
Liv. 2.13.6: inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit
terms.comment: In the midst of a number of things or people: inter ovēs, among the sheep. Inter sē, among themselves, each other: amant inter sē.

terms.gloss: among (a people), in the eyes of
evidence: Cic. Flacc. 31: hoc est apud Graecōs … glōriōsius quam Rōmae triumphāsse
terms.comment: Among a people, in their land or in their opinion: apud Graecōs, among the Greeks (see at the house of).

evidence: Verg. E. 8.56: Orpheus in silvīs, inter delphīnas Arīōn
terms.comment: Of one among many: in prīmīs, among the first, above all.

phrases.latin: nat lupus inter ovēs, fulvōs vehit unda leōnēs
phrases.english: the wolf swims among the sheep, the water carries tawny lions

phrases.latin: Orpheus in silvīs, inter delphīnas Arīōn
phrases.english: an Orpheus in the woods, an Arion among the dolphins

phrases.latin: Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … dux agminis virginum inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit
phrases.english: the girl Cloelia, one of the hostages, … at the head of a band of girls swam the Tiber amid the enemy’s spears

phrases.latin: sūcinum, quod ipsī glēsum vocant, inter vada atque in ipsō lītore legunt
phrases.english: they gather amber, which they call glesum, among the shallows and on the shore itself

phrases.latin: Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt
phrases.english: the two Cicero boys love each other and play games, but they do learn
